text: Reading Passage 2 has seven paragraphs, A-G.
Which paragraph contains the following information?

items: a description of how people misused a bike-sharing scheme <input>
an explanation of why a proposed bike-sharing scheme was turned down <input>
a reference to a person being unable to profit from their work <input>
an explanation of the potential savings a bike-sharing scheme would bring <input>
a reference to the problems a bike-sharing scheme was intended to solve <input>

body.title: Which TWO of the following statements are made in the text about the Amsterdam bike-sharing scheme of 1999?
options: It was initially opposed by a government department.
It failed when a partner in the scheme withdrew support.
It aimed to be more successful than the Copenhagen scheme.
It was made possible by a change in people's attitudes.
It attracted interest from a range of bike designers.

body.title: Which TWO of the following statements are made in the text about Amsterdam today?
options: The majority of residents would like to prevent all cars from entering the city.
There is little likelihood of the city having another bike-sharing scheme.
More trips in the city are made by bike than by any other form of transport.
A bike-sharing scheme would benefit residents who use public transport.
The city has a reputation as a place that welcomes cyclists.

items: The first bike-sharing scheme was the idea of the Dutch group Provo. The people who belonged to this group were <input>. They were concerned about damage to the environment and about <input>, and believed that the bike-sharing scheme would draw attention to these issues. As well as painting some bikes white, they handed out <input> that condemned the use of cars.

However, the scheme was not a great success: almost as quickly as Provo left the bikes around the city, the <input> took them away. According to Schimmelpennink, the scheme was intended to be symbolic. The idea was to get people thinking about the issues.
body.title: The first urban bike-sharing scheme
